profile.headline: Software engineer

positions.title: Software Engineer 2
positions.description:
I work as a software engineer for the ODSP (OneDrive and SharePoint) team developing internal development tools to help drive engineer satisfaction for their engineering toolchain. My work has covered the entire spectrum of the stack, from navigating communication between machines in the datacenter, creating new APIs, and creating frontend experiences. Some of my projects include:
- Modernizing build toolchains for web projects, adding telemetry and accessibility to projects
- Adding new web pages using React to service websites or as extensions to Azure DevOps
- Maintaining and improving Teams chatbot and web-based change tracking tooling to enable engineers to determine where their changes are in deployment
- Worked in C# backend service layer APIs to help report on machine health
- Driving Diversity & Inclusion initiatives within my team and across the broader org, including leading meetings and providing content to discuss and grow together as a team
- Helped mentor over half a dozen (and counting) interns with various web and chat-based projects

positions.title: Software Development Intern
positions.description: I used C# and SQL to develop telecommunications software, with extensive use of tools like Team Foundation Sever and the Microsoft development suite, including SQL Server Management Studio. I also regularly collaborate with remote coworkers through IM/video conferencing software, used virtual machine development environments, and learned Agile development methodology.

positions.title: Software Engineer Intern
positions.description: Added Company News & Events extensible control feature for Dynamics 365 for Talent. This will allow  HR professionals to easily add and edit employee-engaging content, and increase the number of monthly active users on the product. I used client-side JavaScript, HTML, CSS, and learned a proprietary server-side language X++. This project involved extensive work with the UX team and graphic designers in order to create an engaging user experience, and was a highlight of the project.

positions.title: Computer science intern
positions.description: I worked in the Tank Farms division for the second summer. I designed and built two SharePoint websites, each utilized by at least 25 staff members. User manuals for the operation and update of each website were written by me. I also trained end users on the functionality and structure of each SharePoint website.

company.name: US Department of Energy, Office of River Protection

positions.title: Mechanical engineering intern
positions.description:
At the Office of River Protection, I worked in the Tank Farms division. Tank farms store radioactive waste generated from the production of plutonium during World War II. The tanks have degraded over time and retrieval of waste is now a priority to protect the environment. 

At ORP, I helped review proposals, learned about managing projects, helped write fact sheets and presentations for public viewing, and assessed pumps for waste retrieval.

company.name: US Department of Energy contracted by ANR Group

positions.title: Research apprentice
positions.description: Studied the pelagic ecosystem with a team of other students, each of whom conducted a research project. Participated in weekly research cruises to collect data for research, used marine sampling and analysis protocols in the field and laboratory environments. Prepared final research paper and presentation to the laboratory community.

positions.title: Student research assistant, Giachelli Bioengineering Lab
positions.description: Autoclaved materials, prepared solutions, managed general lab upkeep and performed miscellaneous lab duties as assigned. Coordinated with lab members regarding specific tasks.

honors.title: Grace Hopper Celebration of Women in Computing Scholar
honors.description: Awarded full scholarship covering travel, lodging, and registration for the Anita Borg Institute's Grace Hopper Celebration of Women in Computing in Orlando, October 2017.
honors.issuer: Issued by Anita Borg Institute · May 2017

volunteerExperiences.description: I volunteer teach an Introduction to Computer Science course remotely for Douglas High School in Wyoming through the TEALS program. The first semester we teach is SNAP!, a block based programming language. The second semester we teach Python.

I mentored students through a month-long remote internship designed to give them an experience similar to the workplace. After coming up with an initial product, I led the team of students in implementing a prototype of the final version by leading standups, conducting 1:1 meetings with each student and helping answer technical questions.

organizations.name: Human Powered Vehicle (ASME)
organizations.description: Run by ASME, the Human Powered Vehicle Challenge incorporates different kinds of engineering and science in order to make the fastest, most innovative, and safest bicycle. Our bicycle is re-designed yearly and the team works to raise funds for supplies and travel to competition. The competition has speed, endurance, safety, and innovation components. Along with designing the bike for competition, the Human Powered Vehicle team also volunteers in the community with events such as Punkin Chunkin and the Strider World Championships.
